title: What Car Warranty Company Is Worth It
summary: An independent repair shop owner rates which extended warranty companies pay claims fairly, and explains why coverage isn't 100%, why maintenance records matter, and why used-car-lot 'as-is' warranties are weak.

assertions.quote: they are not going to cover 100% of all repairs

verdicts.note: FTC notes buyers may owe a deductible each service visit, and some providers "use a depreciation factor... and pay only partial repair or replacement costs based on your vehicle's mileage" -- confirming coverage is rarely 100%.

assertions.quote: they know that by not maintaining oil level they will deny it for lack of Maintenance it's very easy
you need 90 days or you need 10,000 miles before the coverage actually starts
they may decide well we're only going to cover that part right which could be a piston or a rot out of the whole engine

verdicts.note: Consistent with standard claims-investigation procedures described across multiple sources in this space.

assertions.quote: they sell a cheap policy from a cheap underwriter and there's all kinds of restrictions basically you're going to be on your own

verdicts.note: Curbside/independent used-lot warranties are widely reported as low-value, though 'worthless' overstates; some do provide limited coverage.
